# `silk/schema/shape`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

One description of a `Schema` type's wire form, for everything that needs to know it.

## When to use
Call `silk.schema.schema.Schemas.shape<T>()` to get the [`Shapes`](#Shapes) of `T`: what kind of value
it is on the wire, its fields with their wire names, doc comments and constraints, and its
variants. `silk.schema.json_schema.JsonSchemas` renders it as JSON Schema; command line help
and AI tool definitions read the same description.

## Details
A shape is derived from the type, its `Spec` and its doc comments, never written by hand. Its
parts are nodes of one table, and a part refers to another by [`ShapeRef`](#ShapeRef), so a recursive type
such as a tree whose children are trees is one named node that refers to itself. Every struct and
union is one node named by its type, so a type used twice is described once.

The text in a shape (names, docs, expected text) is static: building one only links nodes.

Import as `Shapes` with `import silk.schema.shape { Shapes }`.

<a id="Constraint"></a>

## `Constraint`

```silk
pub union Constraint
```

A rule a value must follow beyond its type, declared in a `Spec` or given by a codec.

### Details

Every limit is inclusive. Lengths count characters, as JSON Schema's `minLength` and
`maxLength` do, and `usize.MAX` means no upper limit.

<a id="ShapeOf"></a>

## `ShapeOf`

```silk
pub struct ShapeOf<T>
```

The node of a type `T` in a [`Shapes`](#Shapes) table, as `silk.schema.schema.Schema.shape` returns it.

### Details

The type parameter says whose shape it is, so a call of `Schema.shape` names the type it wants
by the result it expects. `at` is the node itself.

<a id="ShapeOf.at"></a>

### Field `at`

```silk
pub at: ShapeRef
```

<a id="Shapes"></a>

## `Shapes`

```silk
pub struct Shapes
```

The shape of one type, and of every type it uses, as a table of nodes.

### When to use

Get one from `Schemas.shape<T>()` and walk it from [`Shapes.root`](#Shapes.impl.root) with [`Shapes.get`](#Shapes.impl.get).

<a id="Shapes.impl.named"></a>

### Method `named`

```silk
pub fn named(self: &Self, name: string<'static>) -> Option<ShapeRef>
```

Returns the node of the named type `name`, if the table has one, finished or pending.

<a id="Shapes.impl.reserve"></a>

### Method `reserve`

```silk
pub effect fn reserve(self: &mut Self, name: string<'static>) -> ShapeRef ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Adds a pending node for the named type `name` and returns its link. Fill it with
[`Shapes.set`](#Shapes.impl.set) once its parts are described; a part that refers back to `name` meanwhile finds
this node with [`Shapes.named`](#Shapes.impl.named).

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot grow the table.

pub fn set(self: &mut Self, at: ShapeRef, shape: Shape) -> ()
```

pub fn nameOf(self: &Self, at: ShapeRef) -> string<'static>
```

Returns the name of the node `at`: its type's name for a struct or union, else empty text.
